figures.caption: Fig. 2. (a) User Profile Shows the multi-domain profiles, demonstrating that our simulator can quickly adapt to new domains. (b) Prompt Optimization Illustrates the automatic prompt optimization process when adapting to a new domain: first, domain adaptation is performed, followed by iterative optimization of the prompt based on interactions with CRS. (c) Simulator. After optimizing the prompt, we integrate it into the simulator and employ an open-ended action generation method to enhance domain adaptability, along with the “think-then-respond” approach to control language style.

Rows correspond to different backbones, while columns report formality, sentiment, conciseness, and carelessness. All values are percentages.

Fig. 4. Human validation of the LLM-as-a-judge protocol. Three senior annotators in the recommender systems domain reviewed the pairwise judgments and marked each case as agreement or disagreement. The left panel reports annotator-wise agreement rates across the three comparison sets, the middle panel summarizes their mean agreement rates and ranges, and the right panel reports pairwise inter-annotator consistency. The results show that all annotators agree with the LLM outputs in more than 60% of cases on average, with moderate-to-high inter-annotator consistency, supporting the reliability of LLM-based evaluation.

Fig. 3. Pairwise win–draw–loss comparison of AdaptSim against three baseline simulators across the Food, Beauty, and Shop domains. Each panel reports six dimensions: naturalness (Nat.), clarity (Cla.), adaptability (Ada.), relevance (Rel.), role-play ability (Rol.), and realism (Rea.). The four settings are AdaptSim with GPT-4omini versus RecUserSim, iEvaLM, and CSHI, and AdaptSim with GPT-3.5-turbo versus RecUserSim. Higher win proportions indicate better performance.

Fig. 1. An illustration of the three core capabilities of an ideal user simulator. (a) Efficient Domain Adaptability: The ability to quickly adapt to new domains with minimal human intervention. (b) Fine-grained User Modeling: The capacity to precisely manipulate the stylistic attributes of generated language. (c) Sufficient Evaluation Validity: The capability to provide an accurate, unbiased, and fine-grained evaluation of a CRS’s performance and robustness.
